Verbeteren van koppelingen met laboratoriumapparatuur en ziekenhuissystemen en automatiseren van handmatige processen.
Samenwerken met eindgebruikers om software te ontwikkelen die aansluit op de dagelijkse praktijk van het laboratorium.
Bewaken van de betrouwbaarheid, stabiliteit en correctheid van het systeem en daarbij moderne AI-tools inzetten tijdens softwareontwikkeling.

Waar ga je werken? 

Je werkt bij Genoomdiagnostiek van de afdeling Klinische Genetica van het LUMC. Miracle wordt dagelijks gebruikt door ongeveer 80 collega’s. Jouw werkplek bevindt zich midden tussen de gebruikers van het systeem. Hierdoor zie je direct hoe de software in de praktijk wordt gebruikt en kun je snel inspelen op nieuwe behoeften.

De werkomgeving is inhoudelijk, pragmatisch en technisch gedreven. Het ontwikkelteam is klein, waardoor je veel invloed hebt op technische keuzes, architectuur en de manier van werken. Samen verbeteren we niet alleen de software, maar ook onze ontwikkelprocessen en de gebruikerservaring.

Hybride werken is mogelijk. Voor het contact met gebruikers en collega’s vinden we aanwezigheid op locatie belangrijk. Daarom werk je minimaal drie dagen per week in het LUMC in Leiden.

De functie is eventueel te combineren met een andere rol binnen het LUMC.

Wat neem je mee? 

Je bent nieuwsgierig naar de techniek achter complexe systemen en vindt het interessant om te begrijpen hoe software in de praktijk wordt gebruikt. Daarbij werk je zorgvuldig en analytisch en neem je verantwoordelijkheid voor de kwaliteit van wat je bouwt. Je schakelt gemakkelijk met eindgebruikers en vertaalt hun vragen naar praktische technische oplossingen.

Of je nu net bent afgestudeerd of al meerdere jaren ervaring hebt: belangrijk is dat je jezelf technisch verder wilt ontwikkelen. Je hoeft daarom niet alle gebruikte technologieën al te beheersen. Wel ben je gemotiveerd om je te verdiepen in bestaande systemen én nieuwe technieken.

Een afgeronde technische HBO- of WO-opleiding.
Ervaring met of interesse in Java, SQL, webontwikkeling, databases en backendontwikkeling.
Affiniteit met softwarearchitectuur, legacy-systemen en moderniseringstrajecten.
Interesse in AI-ondersteunde softwareontwikkeling.
Bij voorkeur ervaring met PostgreSQL, Oracle, PL/SQL of server-side rendering. Ervaring binnen een laboratorium-, zorg- of onderzoeksomgeving is eveneens een pre.


Wat bieden we jou? 

Door gezondheid gedreven; dat is onze missie. Dit geldt uiteraard niet alleen voor onze patiënten maar ook voor onze medewerkers. We streven naar een veilige, inclusieve en gelijkwaardige werkomgeving waarin talentontwikkeling en verbindend leiderschap centraal staan. Om te kunnen blijven leren en ontwikkelen bieden wij interne opleidingen en bijscholing aan.

Daarnaast heb je recht op een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%), vakantiegeld, fietsregeling, sportbudget, thuiswerkvergoeding en een uitstekende reiskostenregeling voor woon-werkverkeer. Ook ben je als medewerker van het LUMC aangesloten bij het ABP-pensioenfonds. Dit betekent dat 70% van je pensioenpremie door het LUMC wordt betaald.

Bekijk alle arbeidsvoorwaarden van het LUMC.

Waar staan wij voor? 

Als academisch medisch centrum streeft het LUMC naar een medewerkersbestand dat een goede afspiegeling is van de samenleving. Wij zetten ons in voor de hoogste kwaliteit op het gebied van gezondheidszorg, onderwijs en (internationaal) onderzoek, waarbij diverse perspectieven van cruciaal belang zijn. Duurzaamheid staat bij ons ook hoog in het vaandel: we zetten ons in voor een gezonde toekomst, niet alleen voor mensen, maar ook voor de planeet.

In lijn met deze waarden willen we een creatieve en inspirerende werkplek zijn, waar het voor ons essentieel is dat iedereen zich thuis, veilig en erkend voelt. Bij ons draait het om wie je bent en wat je bijdraagt, ongeacht je achtergrond. Samen werken wij aan een duurzame en inclusieve toekomst, zowel voor de mensen om ons heen als voor de wereld waarin we leven. Samen zijn wij LUMC.

Job Description:
The Role

Engineering data doesn't organize itself. Behind every plant, platform and vessel sits a mountain of documents, tags and drawings that someone has to make sense of. That someone could be you.

Our Information Management team implements Octave InConcert (formerly SDx) for engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies and owner operators in asset-heavy industries: chemicals and petrochemicals, oil and gas, power, pharma and biotech, food and beverage, utilities and manufacturing. We help EPCs build a complete digital record of a facility as a project moves from design to handover. Then we help owner operators keep that record accurate for the decades the facility runs. That long operating life is where a digital twin really pays off.

As an implementation consultant, you'll turn customer requirements into working solutions. You'll work with solution architects, technical leads, partners and product teams, and you'll spend real time with customers. It's complex work, and that's the appeal. You'll see how a facility's information fits together across its whole lifecycle, and you'll be the person who makes it usable.

What You'll Do

Configure, test and deliver Octave solutions that meet customer requirements on quality, time and budget.
Shape the detailed solution design with your technical lead and write parts of the functional design specification.
Support presales by explaining what an implementation involves and estimating the effort it takes.
Coordinate day-to-day technical work across your project team, including partners and system integrators.
Spot customer solutions that could work for everyone and bring them to our product owners.
Keep up with every product release and pass on what you learn through coaching and knowledge transfer.

Where AI fits in

AI is changing how engineering information gets captured, classified and checked. We already use it every day to configure systems, prepare for customer workshops and deliver solutions more efficiently. InConcert comes with AI built in, so you'll put it to work for customers too. Next up, Octave is building an agentic platform to connect its full portfolio, and you'll be here as it takes shape.

What AI doesn't change: projects succeed because of people. AI can help configure a system, but it can't tell you whether that's the system your customer actually needs. Someone still has to earn the customer's trust, ask the question nobody else thought of and help a team change the way it's worked for 20 years. That's the human part of this job, and it's the part we value most. You'll bring curiosity about new tools and the judgment to know when they help and when they don't.

What You Bring

3+ years delivering enterprise software, engineering data or information management projects
Hands-on experience configuring systems or mapping and migrating data
Confidence with customers, from workshops with engineers to status meetings with project managers
A structured way of working that holds up when you're juggling several tasks
Fluent English, written and spoken
Willingness to travel across Europe, with frequency depending on your project assignments

Nice to have

Experience with InConcert or its predecessor SDx
Knowledge of EPC or operations and maintenance processes in asset-heavy industries
Experience integrating design tools with engineering information systems
Familiarity with cloud environments
Any other European language
A degree in engineering, computer science, information management or a related field

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We hire for potential, and we'll teach you the products.

Why our team

Own your work, start to finish. You'll join more than 25 information management consultants and seven technical leads and architects across Europe and the Middle East. There's a lot of hands-on experience on this team, so you'll always have someone to learn from and plenty of room to grow. Together, we take projects from the first requirements session through implementation, testing, training and go-live. Our managed services keep us close to customers long after handover, so you see what actually works in live operations. Most of us run several customer engagements at once, across different industries and countries. Variety? Plenty. Boredom? Not on this team.

Learn by doing: You'll start with structured training and onboarding, with a mentor of your own to guide you. Early on, you'll join a live delivery team, because nothing teaches you faster than real projects with real customers.
Work your way: When you're not at a customer site, you'll usually work remotely. Prefer a desk to go to? We have offices across Europe too.
Choose your direction: Octave offers a wide range of career paths. From here, you could grow into a technical lead or solution architect role, or move into presales or product.

Octave provides mission-critical software that empowers organizations to make informed decisions across every stage of the asset lifecycle - Design, Build, Operate and Protect - where performance, safety, and reliability are non-negotiable and failure is not an option.

Turning complex operational data into actionable intelligence, Octave connects expertise, real-world conditions and enterprise-scale insight to improve performance, resilience and incident response where it matters most.

Octave has more than 7,000 employees in 45 countries. Learn more at octave.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

All in. Always forward. That's the way we do things around here. We put trust in our people because we believe it's the best way to unleash potential, bring ideas to life, and keep moving ahead. And it's why we're committed to creating an environment that's truly supportive, providing you with the resources you need to support your ambitions, no matter who you are or where you are in the world.

At Octave, we believe that diverse and inclusive teams are critical to the success of our people and our business. Here, everyone is welcome. As an inclusive workplace, we don't discriminate. In fact, we embrace differences and are fully committed to creating equal opportunities, an inclusive environment, and fairness for all.

Respect is the cornerstone of how we operate, so speak up and be yourself. You're valued here.

Job Description

Mars is delivering a global Product Lifecycle Management transformation program (cPLM) to replace our existing system used to capture and evolve knowledge about our products. This role serves as the critical functional bridge between global Packaging R&D, Supply Chain, and the cPLM platform, securing the foundational data integrity of packaging specifications and finished trade items (Intermediate and Above) before and during all FN site deployments. By driving hands-on system validation, enforcing data compliance standards, and directly enabling packaging developers and master data coordinators, this position ensures that structural packaging specifications and logistics data are digitized accurately and compliantly.

In this role, you will work closely with the Food Nutrition (FN) Scope Lead, the FN SMEs and FN cPLM leadership team. You will also occasionally need to collaborate with Enterprise POs, Corporate DT and other segment scope leads to ensure seamless deployment and capability building.

This is a project-role for the Design and Development for the Food cPLM program. The role is funded through June 2028. As we approach the funding end date, your manager will be in touch with additional information including funding for next phases, including pilot and deployment.

Based country: UK or Netherlands

Your Responsibilities

Packaging and Trader Testing & Continuous Improvement

Support Discovery & Workshop Execution: Participate in discovery sessions and workshops, capturing precise user needs, packaging data gaps, process steps, and translating them into clear functional requirements or user stories with the support of the scope leads.
Validate Packaging & Trade Hierarchies: Build, configure, and validate complex packaging structures (primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging levels) and finished trade item specifications in test environments to verify system calculations, palletization patterns, and functional gaps.
Test Attribute Inheritance & Handoffs: Define and execute test cases to ensure packaging material attributes (such as dimensions, weight, recyclability, and barrier properties) accurately roll up and populate at the finished trade item and logistics levels.
Map Regional Variabilities: Connect with Packaging Development, Commercial, and Supply Chain across different regions to capture local packaging material and sourcing variations (e.g., local supplier capabilities, regional transit requirements) and verify that the global cPLM system template supports localized specifications without breaking standardization.
Execute End-to-End Testing (UAT): Support user acceptance testing (UAT) by contributing to test scripts, preparing clean packaging data sets, logging defects, re-testing resolutions, and validating "dual-system" scenarios to ensure downstream systems (like ERP/SAP) receive accurate packaging and trade data.
Drive Process Optimizations: Analyze support ticket trends and user feedback to propose proactive improvements to packaging data structures, workflows, or training templates.

User Support, Learning & Community Enablement

Provide Day-to-Day Functional Support: Act as the primary, hands-on functional expert for Packaging Developers, Graphics/Artwork and MDG teams, troubleshooting complex system blocks (such as packaging specification creation, material BOM linking, and other scenarios).
Triage & Issue Resolution: Capture, log, and categorize user inquiries, rapidly resolving functional "how-to" questions and collaborating with technical partners to resolve deep technical system bugs.
Nurture a Champion Network: Establish and coordinate localized "drop-in" clinics or office hours for packaging and supply chain teams to drive community-led problem-solving and reduce repetitive support tickets.

Training, Deployment & Hypercare Support

Design & Deliver Training: Partner with senior team members and enterprise training leads to support system training, interactive demos, and targeted walk-throughs focused on packaging spec creation, pallet patterns, and trade item setup for developers.
Prepare Stakeholder & Leadership Communications: Translate complex cPLM system changes, updates, and escalation paths into clear, benefits-driven "impact summaries" and presentations for Packaging R&D and/or Supply Chain leadership.
Coordinate Site Deployment Readiness: Drive site-specific deployment checklists, ensuring that local packaging and Master Data teams complete mandatory packaging data-cleansing and training activities before system go-live.
Support FN Pilot and Future Deployments: Support the initial pilot deployment and subsequent Food Nutrition site deployments by establishing reusable templates, checklists, and gathering learning for continuous improvement.
Support On-Site and Virtual Hypercare: Act as the dedicated "Intermediate & Above" hypercare lead during site deployments, working shoulder-to-shoulder with local packaging developers and Master Data analysts to resolve day-one data entry blocks.

Data Quality, Governance & Process Compliance

Audit Legacy Data Readiness: Conduct rigorous data-readiness audits on legacy packaging specifications, pallet specifications, and trade item records, identifying missing, inconsistent, or non-compliant attributes prior to system migration.
Remediate Data Gaps & Create Specifications: Directly support local and regional teams in filling critical data gaps by drafting and creating new packaging component and trade item specifications, obtaining missing dimensions or material properties, and ensuring all key records are complete and enriched prior to data migration.
Partner with Data Stewards: Work closely with global and regional data stewards to define and enforce strict rules for trade item data, ensuring alignment with standards and regional logistics requirements.
Systematically Cleanse Data Gaps: Proactively identify, prioritize, and remediate "orphan" or inconsistent packaging component records, aligning them with the new global packaging taxonomy.
Enforce Global Standardization: Monitor and police adherence to global packaging and trade material standards, escalating unauthorized local workarounds or process deviations.

As the program evolves, your responsibilities may need to shift to support the team where needed most.

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Packaging, Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, Food Science, Food Technology, or a related scientific discipline (preferred)
4-6 years of relevant experience (e.g., R&D, Quality, Supply Chain, Procurement, data or analytics or business support roles)
Interest in digital systems and data; prior experience with R&D/Quality/PLM systems is a plus
Good understanding of packaging R&D processes, material properties (primary/secondary/tertiary), and basic supply chain/logistics flows.
Excellent networker, easily builds rapport remotely
Exceptional English communication skills (oral and written).
Good understanding of using computer systems to do your work. Basic use of AI chat services to support your learning would be useful.
High learning agility with a proven ability to adapt rapidly to changes in a fast-paced, digital transformation environment.
Proven ability to navigate undefined processes and troubleshoot on-the-go.
SAP experience would be highly desirable
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build trust and work effectively with cross-functional, multicultural teams from various R&D, SRA, Procurement, and IT backgrounds.
Exceptional attention to detail with a passion for data accuracy and logical system flows

What can you expect from Mars?

Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.
